title: Counting every piece, spending twice
literal_meaning: The piece-counter uses up twice as much.
explanation: The dictionary’s piece-counter is someone so miserly with food that each cut piece is counted before it is handed to the cook. The saying answers that anxious control with a reversal: the supposed saver ends up using twice as much. “Twice” gives the rebuke its bite; the source supplies no measured account or explanation of how the loss occurs. One editorial application is to a petty economy whose inconvenience creates more expense. The target is grasping control, not careful budgeting when resources are genuinely limited.
meaning_odia: ରାନ୍ଧୁଣିଙ୍କୁ ଦେବା ଆଗରୁ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ପ୍ରତି ଖଣ୍ଡ ଗଣୁଥିବା କୃପଣଙ୍କୁ ଅଭିଧାନ “ଖଣ୍ଡ଼ିଗଣିଆଁ” କହିଛି। ଏତେ ହିସାବ ରଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ତାଙ୍କର ଦୁଇଗୁଣ ସରେ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଫଳରେ କଥାର ମଜା। କେମିତି ଦୁଇଗୁଣ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ହେଲା, ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ଘଟଣା ଦେଇନାହିଁ; ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି କଟାକ୍ଷକୁ ଜୋର ଦିଏ। ଅଳ୍ପ ବଞ୍ଚାଇବାର ଜିଦ୍‌ରେ ଏମିତି ଅସୁବିଧା ତିଆରି ହୋଇପାରେ, ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ପରେ ଅଧିକ ଦେବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ। ଅଭାବରେ ସାବଧାନ ହୋଇ ଚଳିବାକୁ ନୁହେଁ, ଏଠାରେ ଅତି କୃପଣ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣକୁ ହସରେ ଧରାଯାଇଛି।
english_summary: A miser’s minute control is mocked as an economy that can cost more.
odia_summary: ପ୍ରତି ଖଣ୍ଡ ବଞ୍ଚାଇବାର କୃପଣତା ଶେଷରେ ଅଧିକ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର କାରଣ ହେବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: For a shared event, an organiser insists on buying too few paper cups to save a little. When they run out, a volunteer makes a second trip and pays more for a small packet. Someone quotes the saying about the piece-counter. The cups and extra trip are an invented illustration, not the dictionary’s story.
cultural_context: The source explicitly defines food-related miserliness. The broader petty-economy application is editorial. No quantitative spending law, nutritional instruction or judgement of people living in poverty is implied.
